meta.task: Draw a two-step flowchart and export it as a PNG
meta.taskDetail: Two labelled boxes, "Request" and "Review", joined by an arrow, saved as a PNG file.
meta.success: Export produces a PNG of the diagram.
meta.firstValue: A labelled, connected diagram on the canvas.
meta.startingState: New browser profile, no account, empty canvas.
meta.environment: Chrome, 1440 × 900 at 2×, macOS, English UI. Driven by Playwright.
meta.auditType: One task, AI-assisted. The rest of the product is out of scope.
meta.statusNote: PNG export verified with a recorder in place of Chrome's save dialog, which automation cannot see.
meta.author: Draft example generated during prototyping. Findings written from the captured evidence; see Limitations.

journey.response: The dialog stays open. Chrome passes the file to its system save dialog, which automation cannot see. A second run with a recorder in place of that dialog captured a 5,218-byte PNG.

keep.text: Nothing stands between the visitor and the canvas: no account, no template picker, no tour. The labelled diagram existed after 13 interactions.
Double-click to label puts the text centred inside the box, and the arrow attached to both boxes without extra steps.
The export dialog shows a live preview next to four plain options, so the result is visible before saving.

summary.cutNote: Nothing in this flow qualifies. Every step was needed to finish the task.

change.text: Make the flowchart shortcut legible at the moment it applies. It turns five interactions into two and is shown in 1.98:1 grey text.
Tell the user, at export, that a plain PNG cannot be reopened for editing while the drawing itself lives in browser storage.
Keep a pointer to export visible after the first shape is drawn.

next.text: Watch five first-time visitors do this exact task. Record whether they find the flowchart shortcut and the export menu without the welcome hints, then fix finding 1 or 2 first based on what they miss.

findings.title: The fastest route through this task is announced in the faintest text on screen
findings.observed: While a shape is selected, a hint under the toolbar reads "Enter to add text, Cmd + ↑↓ to create a flowchart". It is set at 12 px in rgb(184, 184, 184) on white, a contrast of 1.98:1 (WCAG asks 4.5:1 for text this size). The shortcut works: Cmd + → created the second box and a bound arrow in 2 interactions. Drawing the same box and arrow by hand took 5.
findings.matters: The task asks for exactly what the shortcut produces. The only place the product mentions it is a line most people will not read, so the slower manual route is the default.
findings.hypothesis: First-time users draw connectors by hand and never learn the shortcut. Not observed with real users.
findings.recommendation: Show this hint at body-text contrast (at least 4.5:1) the first time a user draws a second shape, when a flowchart is the likely intent. Leave it quiet afterwards.
findings.evidence: Contrast and size computed from the DOM. Interaction counts from two automated runs. Labelling the second box was not counted in the shortcut path.

findings.title: The hint that points to export disappears before export is needed
findings.observed: On the empty canvas a hand-drawn hint points to the menu button: "Export, preferences, languages, …" (step 1). After the first shape is drawn the hint is gone (steps 2 and 3). Export is reachable only through that menu, as the third item, or with Cmd + Shift + E, which is printed inside the menu. No export control is visible on the canvas, the toolbar or the top bar. The Share button was not tested.
findings.matters: The user reaches the export part of the task after drawing, which is exactly when the guidance has been removed. They must remember the earlier hint or open menus to look.
findings.hypothesis: Some first-time users try Share first, or search the toolbar. Not observed.
findings.recommendation: Once the canvas has content, keep a small persistent pointer to export, or add Export image to the top bar beside Share. A hamburger menu is a common pattern, so validate before changing.
findings.evidence: Hint and menu positions from the DOM on steps 1 and 4. Absence of the hint on steps 2 and 3 seen in the screenshots.
findings.disagreement: A reasonable designer may hold that the menu icon is conventional enough. The finding rests on the hint's removal, not on the menu itself.

findings.title: The exported PNG cannot restore the drawing, and nothing at export says so
findings.observed: The welcome screen states that drawings are saved in browser storage, that storage "can be cleared unexpectedly", and advises saving to a file (step 1). The export dialog has "Embed scene" off by default (step 5). Its tooltip reads: "Scene data will be saved into the exported PNG/SVG file so that the scene can be restored from it. Will increase exported file size." The help icon is the only place this is explained.
findings.matters: Exporting a PNG feels like saving. With the default setting the file is a picture, while the editable drawing stays in storage the product itself calls unreliable.
findings.hypothesis: Some users treat the PNG as their backup and lose the ability to edit when browser data is cleared. Frequency unknown.
findings.recommendation: When the scene exists only in browser storage, turn Embed scene on by default for PNG, or put one line under the PNG button: "This image can't be reopened for editing. Turn on Embed scene to keep it editable." Check the file-size cost first.
findings.evidence: Default state and tooltip text read from the DOM. Storage text from step 1. Data loss itself was not observed.

recommendations.change: Show the flowchart hint at body-text contrast when the second shape is drawn.
checks: Hint text is at least 4.5:1 against the canvas, in light and dark themes
It appears once, on the second shape, and stays quiet afterwards

recommendations.change: Turn Embed scene on by default for PNG while the drawing lives only in browser storage, or explain the default under the PNG button.
checks: Measure the file-size increase on typical scenes
Check how often people reopen exported PNGs to edit them

recommendations.change: Keep a pointer to export visible once the canvas has content.
checks: Five first-time visitors do the task without the welcome hints
Build it only if two or more look for export and do not find it

diagnosis.text: Finding 3 is partly a product question. Where should a no-account user's work live: in the browser, in a file, or in a paid cloud? Each answer changes the export dialog, the welcome copy and the Excalidraw+ offer at once, and settling it takes usage data and business context.
